data.narrative:
Standard Nuclear, a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Kurt Terrani, is evaluated against a comp universe of 11 private and 3 public peers in advanced nuclear. The private peer set includes Fuse Energy, Valar Atomics, Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, and X-Energy; public comparables trade under OKLO, NNE, and SMR.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the company's $182M total raised as a valuation proxy ($470M base), applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $940M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics ($6.0B, Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M, Seed), and Fuse Energy ($200M, Series A)—produces a median valuation of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B.

The two methods triangulate to a valuation range of $687M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $874M. This range reflects meaningful dispersion in peer valuations within the nuclear sector, particularly the wide spread driven by Valar Atomics' late-stage premium. Key uncertainties include the relevance of the Valar comparable given its Series B status and substantially higher valuation, the nascency of public comps in this emerging subsector, and stage-specific capital efficiency assumptions embedded in the step-up multiplier.
